<b>Мягкие ткани свода</b> — пять слоёв:: The soft tissues of the vault form five layers: skin with hair, dense connective tissue with vessels, the galea aponeurotica, loose connective tissue, and the periosteum. Vessels in the dense layer cannot collapse, so scalp wounds bleed heavily. Along the loose layer the scalp slides easily, and hematomas spread there.
<b>Кости свода</b> — наружная и внутренн: The bones of the vault have outer and inner compact plates with spongy diploë between them, which holds red bone marrow and diploic veins. The inner plate is thinner and more brittle. Emissary veins link scalp veins to the sinuses through the bone — a route by which infection can get inside the skull.
<b>Твёрдая мозговая оболочка</b> — плотн: The dura mater is a tough two-layered sheet. Its outer layer is fused to the bone; the inner layer forms folds — the falx cerebri between the hemispheres and the tentorium cerebelli. Where the layers part, the venous sinuses lie between them. Meningeal arteries and nerves run in the dura, so it is sensitive to pain, unlike the brain itself.
<b>Паутинная оболочка</b> — тонкая прозр: The arachnoid mater is a thin transparent film beneath the dura. Threadlike trabeculae run from it to the pia, and between them lies the subarachnoid space, filled with cerebrospinal fluid and the large vessels of the brain. Arachnoid granulations bulge into the sinuses and return the fluid to the blood.
<b>Мягкая оболочка</b> — самая тонкая, о: The pia mater is the thinnest layer. It clings tightly to the brain and dips into every sulcus. Small vessels lie on it; as they enter the brain they carry a sleeve of pia with them, leaving narrow spaces through which cerebrospinal fluid bathes the tissue.
<b>Верхний сагиттальный синус</b> — треу: The superior sagittal sinus is a triangular channel in the dura along the upper edge of the falx. Its walls do not collapse and it has no valves. Cerebral veins drain into it — the bridging veins cross the subarachnoid space and the arachnoid — and cerebrospinal fluid returns through the granulations.
<b>Эпидуральная гематома</b> — кровь меж: An epidural hematoma is blood between the bone and the dura, usually from the middle meningeal artery when the temporal bone is fractured. The blood peels the dura away in a lens shape but does not cross the sutures, where the dura is firmly attached. Typical is a “lucid interval”: the person comes to, then loses consciousness hours later. Urgent surgery is needed.
<b>Субдуральная гематома</b> — кровь меж: A subdural hematoma is blood between the dura and the arachnoid from torn bridging veins. It spreads as a crescent over the surface of the hemisphere and crosses the sutures. In older people and with alcohol use disorder the brain shrinks, the veins are stretched and tear even after a minor injury; a chronic hematoma grows over weeks.
<b>Субарахноидальное кровоизлияние</b> —: Subarachnoid hemorrhage is blood in the subarachnoid space, where it mixes with cerebrospinal fluid and fills the sulci. Without trauma it is most often a ruptured aneurysm of an artery at the base of the brain: a sudden “worst headache of my life,” vomiting, and a stiff neck. Re-rupture and vessel spasm make it dangerous.
<b>Верхний сагиттальный синус</b> идёт п: The superior sagittal sinus runs along the upper edge of the falx from the crista galli to the internal occipital protuberance. Superior cerebral veins drain into it, and cerebrospinal fluid returns through the granulations. At the back it joins other sinuses at the confluence of sinuses.
<b>Нижний сагиттальный синус</b> идёт по: The inferior sagittal sinus runs along the free lower edge of the falx above the corpus callosum. It joins the great cerebral vein (of Galen), which collects blood from the deep parts of the brain, and continues as the straight sinus — along the line where the falx meets the tentorium — to the confluence.
<b>Поперечные синусы</b> идут от стока в: The transverse sinuses run sideways from the confluence along the edge of the tentorium, then curve into an S shape (the sigmoid sinuses) and pass through the jugular foramina into the internal jugular veins. The right one is usually larger. The sigmoid sinus lies right behind the mastoid air cells, so mastoiditis can cause its thrombosis.
<b>Пещеристый синус</b> — венозное сплет: The cavernous sinus is a venous plexus on each side of the sella turcica. The internal carotid artery passes through it together with the abducens nerve (VI), while nerves III, IV, V₁, and V₂ lie in its lateral wall. The ophthalmic veins drain into it from the front, so an infection in the “danger triangle” of the face can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis.
<b>Верхний и нижний каменистые синусы</b: The superior and inferior petrosal sinuses carry blood backward from the cavernous sinus: the superior along the ridge of the petrous temporal bone to the transverse sinus, the inferior to the jugular foramen. The intercavernous sinuses link the right and left cavernous sinuses around the pituitary.
<b>От кожи до коры</b> — около сантиметр: From skin to cortex is about a centimeter: scalp, bone, and three meninges. The dura is fused to the bone, the arachnoid lies against the dura, and the pia clings to the brain. Between the arachnoid and the pia is the subarachnoid space with cerebrospinal fluid, in which the brain seems to float. Layer thicknesses in the section are altered for clarity. Choose a layer.
<b>Синусы твёрдой оболочки</b> — каналы: The dural venous sinuses are channels between the layers of the dura that drain blood from the brain to the internal jugular veins. Their walls do not collapse, and they have no valves. Almost all the blood meets at the confluence at the back of the head, then leaves for the neck through the transverse and sigmoid sinuses. Choose a sinus.
Мозг окружён тремя оболочками и плавает: The brain is wrapped in three membranes and floats in cerebrospinal fluid, while its blood drains through rigid channels in the dura — the sinuses. Here you can also see why bleeding above and below the dura looks and behaves so differently.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The meninges — dura, arachnoid, and pia — continue into the vertebral canal and surround the spinal cord. The dura of the skull is fused to the bone and forms partitions: the falx cerebri between the hemispheres, the tentorium over the cerebellum, the falx cerebelli, and the diaphragma sellae over the pituitary.

The dural sinuses collect blood from the brain, eyes, middle ear, and skull bones. Through emissary and ophthalmic veins they are connected with the veins of the face and scalp.

How it works

Cerebrospinal fluid (about 150 mL) is made by the choroid plexuses of the ventricles — about 500 mL a day, so it is renewed 3–4 times. From the ventricles it flows into the subarachnoid space, bathes the brain and spinal cord, and is absorbed into the venous sinuses through the arachnoid granulations. Floating in this fluid, the brain weighs not 1.4 kg but about 50 g.

Medicine

  • Meningitis is inflammation of the pia and arachnoid: headache, fever, and a stiff neck. Bacterial meningitis is life-threatening; vaccines exist against the main pathogens.
  • Epidural and subdural hematomas and subarachnoid hemorrhage are told apart on CT by shape: a lens, a crescent, and blood in the sulci and cisterns.
  • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis is a rare cause of stroke in young people: during pregnancy, with hormonal contraceptives, or with dehydration.
  • Lumbar puncture: cerebrospinal fluid is drawn with a needle below the end of the spinal cord — between the 3rd and 4th or the 4th and 5th lumbar vertebrae.
  • Headache often comes from the meninges and their vessels: the brain itself feels no pain.

Simplifications

  • Layer thicknesses in the section are altered: the meninges and the subarachnoid space are shown thicker than they really are. The sinuses are smooth tubes of uniform cross-section; the falx and tentorium are translucent sheets; the choroid plexuses and cerebral veins other than a bridging vein and the great cerebral vein are not shown. Blood flow is sped up.
